mechanism_narrative: If residential time keeps easing while workplaces and transit remain less suppressed, people are spending more hours outside home and converting that regained out-of-home time into discretionary shopping trips, so RETAIL_REC should rise over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed positive while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remained below baseline in the snapshot
failure_condition: The hypothesis fails if RETAIL_REC does not increase relative to the prior 28-day mean even when RESIDENTIAL stays below its current level or WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both continue moving toward baseline for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in PARKS mobility redirects leisure time from outdoor recreation to indoor retail and dining trips, so a further PARKS decline should lift RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below -25 and remains there for at least one weekly mean
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from -16.1 at t-1w to -37.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC does not rise within 14 days after PARKS crosses below -25, or if RETAIL_REC falls while PARKS remains depressed.

mechanism_narrative: When transit mobility recovers from extreme suppression, access to shopping districts improves and retail visits follow with a lag, so a sustained TRANSIT rebound should push RETAIL_REC higher over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises by at least 5 points week-on-week from a level below -55
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -67.0 to -57.0 across the snapshot window
failure_condition: The claim fails if TRANSIT rises by 5 or more points from below -55 and RETAIL_REC still does not exceed its prior 28-day mean over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained drop in WORKPLACES mobility releases weekday time for errands and shopping, so lower workplace attendance should translate into higher retail mobility over the next month.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES stayed below baseline in every weekly mean and improved to -22.7 at t-0w
failure_condition: Reject if WORKPLACES remain below baseline but RETAIL_REC continues to average below its last-28-day mean over the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The combined condition of higher grocery/pharmacy trips and lower park use signals substitution toward practical errands and away from outdoor leisure, which should support modest retail gains within one week.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stayed positive while PARKS turned sharply more negative at t-0w
failure_condition: The interaction is rejected if RETAIL_REC does not improve within 7 days during weeks when GROCERY_PHARM is above baseline and PARKS is below -20.

mechanism_narrative: If residential mobility stops rising and transit remains deeply suppressed, the area is still constrained by mobility frictions, so retail visits will stay weak or fall over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -50 while RESIDENTIAL stays below +10
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT is persistently near -60 while RESIDENTIAL is only moderately positive
failure_condition: The hypothesis fails if RETAIL_REC rises above its prior 28-day mean despite TRANSIT staying below -50 and RESIDENTIAL staying below +10 for at least two weekly observations.

mechanism_narrative: A late-spring normalization pattern should gradually lift retail mobility as outdoor activity stabilizes and commuting resumes, producing a slow increase in RETAIL_REC over the next month even without a sharp trigger.
evidence_refs: fact:The snapshot ends in mid-November, a period when seasonal mobility shifts are plausible
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC remains flat or declines over the next 28 days while PARKS and TRANSIT both continue recovering from their current lows.

mechanism_narrative: If transit and workplaces rebound together from their current depressed levels, the joint return of commuting and central-area foot traffic will spill into retail visits after a two-week lag.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both rise by at least 3 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -67.0 to -57.0 while WORKPLACES improved from -31.0 to -22.7 in the snapshot
failure_condition: The mechanism is false if simultaneous weekly gains in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES do not precede a higher RETAIL_REC average within 14 days.
